clips.send: Athens. The first state-chartered public university. The legislature chartered the University of Georgia on January 27, 1785. Abraham Baldwin, who wrote the charter, was its first president. Classes began in 1801 at Franklin College on 633 acres given by John Milledge. The town was named Athens after the ancient Greek center of learning.

clips.send: Brier Creek. A Patriot defeat after Kettle Creek. Just weeks after Kettle Creek, British troops surprised a Patriot army camped at Brier Creek. Hundreds of Patriots were killed, captured or drowned trying to escape across the creek and swamps. The defeat let the British keep their hold on most of Georgia through 1779.

clips.send: Kettle Creek. Georgia’s great Patriot victory. About 700 Loyalists under Colonel John Boyd were marching to join the British at Augusta. About 400 Patriot militia under Andrew Pickens, John Dooly and Elijah Clarke surprised their camp in Wilkes County. Boyd was mortally wounded; casualties were about 21 Patriots and 115 Loyalists (estimates). Austin Dabney, a free Black artilleryman, was badly wounded here and later honored by the state.

clips.send: Nancy Hart’s cabin. A frontier legend. Nancy Hart lived with her family near the Broad River in what is now Elbert County. Legend: Loyalist soldiers forced her to cook them a meal; she hid their guns and held them prisoner until help came. The story was written down years later, so historians treat the details as legend. Hart County and the town of Hartwell are named for her — the only Georgia county named for a woman.

clips.send: Savannah. Liberty Boys, a British capture and a failed siege. Liberty Boys met at Tondee’s Tavern in 1774–75 to protest British laws. The Declaration of Independence was read aloud here on August 10, 1776. British troops captured Savannah on December 29, 1778 and held it until July 1782. On October 9, 1779 a French-American attack on the British lines failed; Casimir Pulaski was mortally wounded.

clips.send: Augusta. Changed hands again and again. The British occupied Augusta in early 1779, left, and returned in 1780. Elijah Clarke attacked it in September 1780 but had to retreat. On June 5, 1781 Patriots under Pickens, Clarke and Henry Lee forced the British to surrender Augusta. Georgia’s government met here from 1786 until the capital moved to Louisville in 1796.

clips.send: Midway and Sunbury. Georgia’s most eager Patriots. St. John’s Parish sent Dr. Lyman Hall to the Continental Congress in 1775, before the rest of Georgia joined. clips.send: 奥古斯塔。几度易手。1779 年初英军占领奥古斯塔，随后撤离，1780 年又卷土重来。 1780 年 9 月以利亚·克拉克进攻这里，但被迫撤退。 1781 年 6 月 5 日，皮肯斯、克拉克和亨利·李率领的爱国者迫使英军交出奥古斯塔。 1786 年起州政府在这里办公，直到 1796 年首府迁往路易斯维尔。

clips.send: 凯特尔溪。佐治亚爱国者的大胜。约 700 名效忠派在约翰·博伊德上校率领下，正赶往奥古斯塔与英军会合。 约 400 名爱国者民兵在安德鲁·皮肯斯、约翰·杜利和以利亚·克拉克率领下，在威尔克斯县突袭了他们的营地。 博伊德身受致命伤；伤亡估计为爱国者约 21 人、效忠派约 115 人。 非裔炮兵奥斯汀·达布尼在这里身受重伤，后来受到州政府表彰。

clips.send: 南希·哈特的小屋。边疆传奇。南希·哈特一家住在布罗德河附近，即今天的埃尔伯特县。 传说：效忠派士兵逼她做饭，她偷偷藏起他们的枪，把他们扣押到救兵赶来。 这个故事是多年后才被写下来的，所以历史学家把细节视为传说。 哈特县和哈特维尔市都以她命名——这是佐治亚唯一以女性命名的县。
